questions.q: What does James 1:22–25 compare the hearer who does nothing to?
options: A builder without tools
Someone who looks in a mirror, walks away and forgets what they saw
A farmer who never sows
A sleeping watchman
questions.explanation: It is a precise description of the post-retreat dip: three days of seeing yourself clearly, then a week in which the image fades because nothing was done with it.

questions.q: What does the chapter highlight about Nehemiah's sequence (Nehemiah 1–2)?
options: He resigned immediately and announced his plan
He prayed for a sign before doing anything
Insight, then time; a specific plan; a quiet look at the facts before announcing; work broken into pieces people could do
He acted alone without telling anyone
questions.explanation: He wept and prayed for days, waited months for the right moment, inspected the walls at night, then divided the work. The opposite of coming home and announcing everything on the first evening.

questions.q: At what pace should the Act cards be done?
options: All of them in the first week
Only after all Share cards are done
One per day
Roughly one a week, starting with the Session Ten action card
questions.explanation: The point is not speed. It is that the cards leave the pile and become things that happened.

questions.q: What three things does the chapter say to include when asking someone to share a burden?
options: This is the burden; this is how I have been carrying it alone; this is the specific help I am requesting
How long you have suffered, how badly, and who is to blame
A Bible verse, a prayer, and a deadline
Your intention, your rule of life, and your cards
questions.explanation: Specific requests are easier to answer than general appeals, and a request allows the other person to answer honestly. Expect that some will say no.

questions.q: What is the Seek-counsel card 'done' when?
options: When the decision is made
When the date of the appointment is in the diary, or the next available access step is completed
When your pastor approves
When the problem is solved
questions.explanation: Not the decision; the appointment. If you cannot book immediately, join a waiting list, ask for a referral, or find out the cost. Do not let an unavailable appointment become no action.

questions.q: What is the aim of the 'Jethro conversation'?
options: To confess your failures to a leader
To find a new job
To ask the five structural questions and then request one structural change from whoever can change something
To plan your next retreat
questions.explanation: Rest does not fix a structure. Jethro's advice to Moses in Exodus 18 was: you are doing too much, some of it can be done by others, here is how to divide it.

reflection: Which Act card will you do this week? Write the day.
Which Share card, what kind of sharing does it need, and what exactly will you ask for? Write the three sentences.
Which Seek-counsel appointment or access step, and when will you make the call?
Answer the five Jethro questions. Then name the person you will take them to, and the one structural change you will request, if capacity allows.
